design:
D1 Every request model inherits `RequestModel` (`hub/hub/schemas/common.py`, `extra="forbid"`), so strictness is the default rather than a per-model decision.

D2 Exemptions live in `hub/tests/test_request_strictness.py` as `LAX_BY_DESIGN` (today: the spec document payload, forward compatible by its own requirement) and `NO_CONTRACT_BY_DESIGN` (today: `patch_agent`, which refuses unknown keys by hand with 400), each with a reason that the suite also asserts is present.

D3 Legacy translation subtracts the whole vocabulary (`LEGACY_CONTEXT_VOCABULARY` in `hub/hub/schemas/agents.py`, assignee aliases in `hub/hub/schemas/tasks.py`) and starts from the residue, so `forbid` judges everything else.

limits: The check is a test run in CI, not a runtime report; a route added without running the suite is unchecked until it is.

lifecycle: Imported from openspec 2026-10-07; overhauled 2026-10-08 against the code at e25e059.
problem: A field silently discarded tells the caller they were understood when they were not; when the field was a supervision posture, the run is already executing unsupervised by the time the response is read (F116). A timestamp without a zone is likewise read as a different instant on a machine in another zone.

requirements.rationale: The Hub cannot tell a typo from a field that changes behaviour; only the caller can, and only if told. One policy across routes means no route looks safe by accident.
requirements.statement: A write request whose body carries a field its contract does not declare SHALL be refused, and the refusal SHALL name the field, on every route alike.

requirements.rationale: An exemption without a reason is indistinguishable from the rule never having been applied.
requirements.statement: A request contract MAY accept undeclared fields only where its own requirement demands it, and SHALL then be listed with its reason among the declared exemptions; a body accepted as an untyped mapping SHALL likewise be listed with its reason and SHALL refuse unknown keys by name itself.

requirements.rationale: A translation that rebuilds the body from the names it knows drops the rest silently, reintroducing the failure inside the mechanism meant to prevent it; one that removes only the name it read refuses a rolling upgrade's second alias.
requirements.statement: A contract that translates a superseded vocabulary before validation SHALL remove every name that vocabulary defines, including names nothing reads any more, and SHALL carry every other field forward to be refused, so that a request carrying two legacy names for one value is accepted and a field outside both vocabularies is refused by name.

requirements.rationale: The rule fails by omission, so a one-time check decays at the next route; deriving the list from routing makes a new route covered by construction.
requirements.statement: The test suite SHALL derive every write route from the application's routing table and fail when a body model, or any model nested in it, tolerates extra fields, or a route declares no body model, unless it is a listed exemption with a reason.

requirements.rationale: SQLite stores no zone; a bare timestamp is read as local time by browsers and was shown an hour off on a UTC+1 machine.
requirements.statement: Every timestamp the Hub returns SHALL state its zone (UTC), and the app SHALL show it as that instant whatever the operator's machine's zone.

requirements.rationale: overhaul-route-shadow-names (F248): refuse at creation only, Hub-only, so an existing agent that holds the word is not stopped by a check at every use site.
requirements.statement: Every Hub door that creates an agent row MUST refuse a name that a route registered before the agent's own routes would answer for (today conflicts, settings and sessions, compared case-insensitively), with a sentence naming that route; no check outside agent creation MUST refuse such a name.

requirements.rationale: AgentTaskCreate re-validates through TaskCreate inside the handler (agent_actions.py:245); a TaskCreate-only check would answer 500 at the agent door.
requirements.statement: Creating a task through the operator door, the agent door or a loop's initial tasks MUST refuse an id that a route registered before GET /tasks/{task_id} would answer for (today board and boards, case-insensitively) with a 422 naming id, never a 500.

requirements.rationale: The queue and sessions collisions existed when F248 was filed and nobody saw them; a list is only durable if the route table checks it.
requirements.statement: The Hub's tests MUST fail, naming the route and the word, when a route with a fixed segment is registered before a route whose caller-named parameter at that segment it matches over the whole path, unless the word is refused for that parameter's resource or the parameter is Hub-minted (runner_id, the UI catch-all full_path).

in_scope: Before-validators that translate legacy field names
The declared exemptions and the test that enforces the rule over the routing table
The zone of every returned timestamp and how the app displays it
non_goals: Validation of field values: owned by each route's capability

summary: What the Hub's HTTP surface promises about the data that crosses it. A body field the receiving contract does not declare is refused by name, uniformly; the few contracts that decline the rule say why; legacy vocabularies are translated without swallowing unknown fields; a test over the routing table catches any route that slips; and every timestamp the Hub returns states its zone and is shown as that instant.
